critical_code_review_comments: Services.jsx (line 56): override.catalogs = [] correctly clears defaults but means admin cannot 'partially override' — they must either fully replace defaults or reset. This is the documented behavior per the PR notes; acceptable.
ServicesManager.jsx handleCatalogUpload (line 43): client-side .pdf extension check is correct; backend whitelist also enforces .pdf. Defense-in-depth OK.

Backend /api/uploads (server.py line 246): allows .mp4/.mov/.gif uploads via the same endpoint admin uses for catalogs — frontend filters to .pdf so this is fine, but a dedicated /api/uploads/catalog endpoint with PDF-only enforcement would be cleaner for future hardening. Non-blocking.

Backend has no file-size limit on /api/uploads — a malicious authenticated admin could upload arbitrarily large files. Consider a max-size guard (e.g. 25MB). Low priority since only authenticated admin can upload.

ServicesManager.jsx (line 100): useEffect re-runs startEdit on every overrides change which re-seeds draft and silently discards unsaved edits if overrides re-fetch finishes after user starts editing. Minor UX edge case.
